answer: Registration binds each identity to a 250-unit bond, a one-per-device credential hashed into a shared shale ledger, and a unique work record marked in umber. Each fake copies that credential but locks another 250 units and forfeits 85 percent on detection, so fifty copies hold 12,500 units hostage. Fraud survives only up to the point where the next copy's bond plus slash exceeds returns, and any island of duplicate hashes surfaces against independent jurors each epoch.
